draw: CONCEPT member draws only. The RELATION previews are a different population at a different column set on a different schedule, and they are recorded beside their own cuts in the data plane — see `relation_record`, which is a POINTER and never a copy: no fact appears in both records
blocks_per_concept: ONE ENTRY PER GROUNDING SOURCE. `stem` repeats for a concept that grounds on more than one relation; the unique key is (stem, source_index) and `source_count` is how many the concept DECLARES, so a stem with fewer entries than its source_count has a source that could not be drawn — see `concept_refused`

concept_draw.columns: exactly the concept page's Fields table, in its order, from sdk/project/mac_okf.py#_grounding_fields — the sample shows ONLY the columns the concept declares
concept_draw.population: the concept's OWN members: grounding.value_filter where declared, else grounding.discriminator IS NOT NULL, else the whole host relation — read through tools/mac_generate_ontology_tests.py#member_population, the same function the identity family is narrowed by
concept_draw.order: md5('<seed>' || '|' || every declared cell CAST to text, in column order) ASC, then every declared column ASC NULLS LAST as the tie-break; the rendered rows are then sorted lexicographically for the file's bytes
concept_draw.reproducibility: the draw is a pure function of (seed, the row's declared cells) and NOT an engine RNG: no engine promises setseed/USING SAMPLE is stable across its own versions. Same seed + same data => same rows, per engine, across runs and versions; cross-engine only where CAST(x AS VARCHAR) agrees

samples.population_rule: a STRATIFIED window of up to 40 row(s) over the member rows, outer-joined onto the 11 member(s) the concept DECLARES: EVERY member appears at least once — each member's first row, in the seeded order, before any member's second — and the budget that remains is spent going round the members again in that same order. A declared member with NO row in the data still appears, carrying its `Brand` and empty cells; where the members outnumber the window it is one row per member as far as the limit reaches, and the record states both counts, over the rows where "Brand" IS NOT NULL (grounding.discriminator: Brand)
samples.columns_from: sdk/project/mac_okf.py#_grounding_fields — the concept page's own Fields table, in its order
samples.member_grain_basis: the concept declares a members: block, so its members are the distinct values of its canonical key `Brand`; the window is drawn STRATIFIED over those members rather than collapsed to one row each — every member gets a row, and the rest of the budget goes back to the data
